title: JUCE VST Plugin Development Playbook
description: End-to-end development playbook for building creative unique VST audio plugins with JUCE and AI assistance. Covers the full plugin lifecycle from concept through release: spec development, DSP architecture, implementation, GUI, testing, DAW validation, optimization, and release. Designed for a single developer retaining full creative control with AI handling code generation, review, and validation. Each phase is gated — nothing advances until acceptance criteria are met.
extracted_from: conversation_full.md — single 24,292-line session building Epiphany Machine VST v3, plus user gap-analysis answers and v2 spec template, plus deep crawl of melatonin.dev, awesome-juce, JUCE docs, Pamplejuce, SimpleCompressor
changelog_v2: Added: references section with JUCE/DSP/community links, cross-platform build targets (all OS), automated test framework, Reaper DAW testing procedures, state save/restore as required phase, optimization/hardening phase (filled from best practices), retrospective phase (filled), 14 missing validation steps promoted to checklist items, prevention rules wired as pre-flight checks, v2 spec as template reference, distribution workflow
changelog_v3: Fixed: failure mode numbering (session bugs now EM-xx, generic FM-xx), wavefolder formula consistency, smoothing time distinction (20ms params / 42ms bypass). Added: community libraries (chowdsp_utils detailed, Gin, sst-filters, signalsmith-stretch, ff_meters), tooling details (pluginval strictness, Perfetto, melatonin_inspector), GUI performance patterns (VBlankAttachment, setOpaque, setBufferedToImage, JUCE_LIVE_CONSTANT), cross-platform specifics (MSVC static linking, AU cache reset), CI matrix details from Pamplejuce (sccache, universal binary, Inno Setup, notarytool), AsyncUpdater NOT lock-free warning, hidden allocation warning (unordered_map::find), two-stage review methodology, boundary condition verification process

roles.you: Creative director, sound designer, final decision-maker on all audio/UX choices. You define WHAT the plugin does and HOW it should sound. Every creative decision is human_only — AI asks, never assumes.
roles.ai: Code architect, implementation engine, reviewer, test generator. AI handles HOW to build what you've defined. Never makes creative decisions autonomously. Must ask for creative direction, never propose defaults for sound/naming/aesthetics.

references.description: Documentation, guides, and community resources. Feed relevant links as context per phase.

project.v2_spec_template: claude-code-prompt-epiphany-machine-v2-FINAL.md — use as structural template for future plugin specs. Contains: architecture overview, DSP implementation details, GUI design spec, parameter list, preset system, build instructions, test checklist.

api_modules.description: JUCE module documentation index. Key modules: juce_audio_processors, juce_dsp, juce_gui_basics, juce_audio_basics, juce_audio_plugin_client

api_classes.description: Alphabetical JUCE class reference. Key classes: AudioProcessor, AudioProcessorValueTreeState, AudioProcessorEditor, SmoothedValue, AudioBuffer, Component, LookAndFeel_V4, Timer, NormalisableRange
api_classes.when_to_use: Any implementation phase — look up specific class APIs

tutorials.description: Official JUCE tutorials. Key tutorials: 'Create a basic Audio/MIDI plugin', 'DSP module', 'Customise the look and feel', 'Slider values'

awesome_juce.description: Comprehensive curated list of JUCE resources: open-source plugins, libraries, templates, tutorials, tools. Deep-crawl this for reference implementations, testing frameworks, CI templates, and DSP libraries.
awesome_juce.when_to_use: Phase 2 (find reference implementations), Phase 3 (CI templates), Phase 11 (optimization techniques)

melatonin_blog.description: Expert JUCE blog by Sudara. Covers: testing with Catch2, CI/CD for JUCE, audio thread debugging, LookAndFeel patterns, JUCE best practices. Highly relevant to automated testing and optimization phases.
key_articles: How to add Catch2 testing to a JUCE project
Setting up GitHub Actions for JUCE

stanford_320c.description: Stanford CCRMA — Audio DSP Projects in Faust and C++. Covers: FDN reverbs, filters, delay effects, granular synthesis, spectral processing.
stanford_320c.when_to_use: Phase 4 (DSP implementation) — reference for algorithm correctness

key_authors: Julius O. Smith III — Physical Audio Signal Processing (FDN reverbs, delay networks) — https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/
Vadim Zavalishin — The Art of VA Filter Design (Cytomic TPT SVF, all filter topologies) — free PDF
Andy Simper (Cytomic) — original TPT SVF papers — https://cytomic.com/files/dsp/
Will Pirkle — Designing Audio Effect Plugins in C++ (practical JUCE-adjacent DSP)

chowdsp_utils.description: 30+ modules of production-quality DSP and plugin utilities. Key modules: chowdsp_filters (Butterworth, Chebyshev, Elliptic, SVF), chowdsp_waveshapers (ADAA hard/soft clip, tanh, wavefolding), chowdsp_reverb (FDN templates), chowdsp_sources (anti-aliased oscillators), chowdsp_plugin_state (faster APVTS replacement), chowdsp_presets (preset management).
chowdsp_utils.when_to_use: Phase 4 — before implementing custom DSP, check if chowdsp has it already. Especially for ADAA waveshaping (avoids oversampling cost) and anti-aliased oscillators.

notable: Gin (FigBug) — large utility collection, StackBlur, websockets — github.com/FigBug/Gin
sst-filters — Surge synthesizer filters as standalone library — github.com/surge-synthesizer/sst-filters

pluginval.description: Cross-platform plugin validator. Strictness levels 1 (basic) to 10 (comprehensive). Level 5+ recommended for release.
pluginval.tests: Editor open/close cycles, state save/restore round-trip, parameter randomization, audio processing stress, listener cleanup, CPU measurement
pluginval.debugging: Run pluginval from IDE with debugger. Note random seed from CI output to reproduce intermittent issues.

perfetto.description: Cross-platform performance tracer. Shows every callback in sequence (not aggregated). Critical for audio thread where worst-case matters.
perfetto.setup: Add melatonin_perfetto module. Annotate with TRACE_DSP, TRACE_COMPONENT macros. Output .pftrace → ui.perfetto.dev

melatonin_inspector.description: Web-inspector-style tool for JUCE component debugging. Inspect hierarchy, bounds, visibility, repaint regions.
melatonin_inspector.when_to_use: Phase 7 (GUI) for debugging layout and repaint issues

reaper_vst_testing.description: Reaper DAW testing workflow: Options → Preferences → Plug-ins → VST → Add path to ~/.vst3 → Rescan. Load plugin on track, verify GUI, automate parameters, save/reopen session.

superpowers_mapping.brainstorming: Use in Phase 0 to develop the plugin concept and spec. AI asks multi-choice questions, user picks options.
superpowers_mapping.writing_plans: Use in Phase 2 to produce the architecture doc and task breakdown.
superpowers_mapping.subagent_driven_development: Preferred for implementation phases. Fresh subagent per task with two-stage review (spec compliance then code quality). Caught critical bugs implementers missed.
superpowers_mapping.security_review: Use to review any new skills or external code before integrating.

integration_notes.spec_template: Use the v2 spec (claude-code-prompt-epiphany-machine-v2-FINAL.md) as a structural template for new plugin specs. It covers: architecture overview with signal flow diagram, DSP implementation with exact algorithms, GUI design with pixel dimensions and color palette, complete parameter list, preset system, build instructions, and a final test checklist.
integration_notes.session_history: After each completed phase, extract the working conversation into a phase summary. This becomes the context seed for the next phase — prevents token waste from carrying full history.

checklists.title: Phase 0: Plugin Concept & Spec
checklists.purpose: Define exactly what you're building before writing any code. The AI should be ASKING YOU questions here, not proposing solutions.

items.title: Define plugin type and signal flow
items.ai_role: interviewer — ask multi-choice questions for each decision
items.description: AI prompts for: plugin type (synth/effect/analyzer/hybrid), signal flow (mono/stereo, sidechain?), DSP chain (processing blocks and order), parameter count estimate. User answers each. AI NEVER proposes a signal flow unprompted.
items.reference: v2 spec template: ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW section shows the signal flow format

items.title: Define the sound identity
items.description: What should this plugin SOUND like? User provides: reference plugins/hardware, genre context, character words, what makes it different. AI records these exact words as the creative north star. AI never paraphrases or reinterprets.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session1: AI proposed generic preset names and user rejected them. ALWAYS use user's exact creative language.

items.title: Define technical constraints
items.description: Lock down: JUCE version, target formats (VST3/AU/AAX/Standalone), target OS (ALL: Linux, macOS, Windows), target DAW (Reaper), sample rates (44.1k-192kHz), buffer size range, CPU budget. AI flags issues with choices.

items.title: Gain staging design
items.ai_role: advisor — identify existing gain staging issues
items.description: Define when hot signals are OK vs not OK. From Epiphany Machine session: 'don't make it run too hot, but we want the effect to be intense. without drive the effect shouldn't be overly hot though.' AI should audit existing gain staging before proposing changes.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session1: 6 layers of conservative gain staging identified as root cause of 'effect not noticeable enough'. Always audit existing gain staging early.

items.title: Preset theme and naming
items.ai_role: drafter — but user has FINAL say on every name
items.description: AI will suggest generic names. REJECT THEM. User defines creative direction and approves every name individually.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session1: AI proposed 'Superposition, Entanglement, Dark Matter' — user rejected as too generic. Always ask user for creative naming direction first.

items.title: Write the one-page spec
items.description: AI compiles everything into a structured spec doc following the v2 spec template format: architecture overview with signal flow diagram, DSP algorithms with code snippets, GUI design with dimensions and colors, parameter list with ranges and defaults, preset system, build instructions, test checklist, 'what not to do' section.

items.title: Spec self-review
items.description: Before user reviews, AI checks for: placeholder values, contradictions, ambiguity, scope gaps, formula correctness. From session: caught wavefolder bypass bug, MORPH label ambiguity, parameter count error in self-review.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session2: Wavefolder formula sin(x*PI)/1.0 amplifies by PI at drive=0. Always verify formulas at boundary conditions (param=0, param=1, param=max).

items.title: PHASE GATE: Spec approved
gate_conditions: Plugin type and signal flow defined
Sound identity documented in YOUR words (not paraphrased by AI)
Technical constraints locked (JUCE version, formats, ALL target OS, Reaper DAW)
Preset theme chosen with creative names you approve

checklists.title: Phase 1: Performance Audit (if upgrading existing code)
checklists.purpose: Before ANY new features, audit the existing codebase for memory/CPU/thread-safety issues. Skip this phase for brand-new plugins.

items.title: Thread safety audit
items.description: Scan for non-atomic shared state between audio and GUI threads. Use std::atomic<bool> for all flags shared between threads.
items.prevention_rule: EM-01: PresetManager had plain bool shared between threads. Always use std::atomic for cross-thread state.

items.title: Instance isolation audit
items.description: Check for static variables shared across plugin instances. All state must be per-instance members.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session3: static int lastPreset was shared across all instances.

items.title: Audio thread allocation audit
items.description: Search for heap allocations, large memsets, or std::string construction on the audio thread.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session3: GlitchEngine cleared 1MB buffer on audio thread. Also: std::unordered_map.find() can allocate via std::string construction — use std::vector<std::pair<>> for audio-thread lookups.

items.title: Parameter lookup optimization
items.description: Check for O(N) parameter lookups on the audio thread. Cache parameter indices at init time.
items.prevention_rule: EM-01: First cache attempt keyed on names (still O(N) to compute key). Verify ENTIRE call chain is O(1).

items.title: PHASE GATE: Performance audit complete
gate_conditions: No non-atomic shared state between audio/GUI threads
No static variables shared across instances
No heap allocations in processBlock path
Parameter lookups are O(1) on audio thread

checklists.title: Phase 2: Architecture & Task Breakdown
checklists.purpose: Turn the spec into a buildable plan with complete code.

items.title: Read all existing source files
items.description: AI must read EVERY source file before planning. No planning from memory.

items.title: Design class architecture
items.description: Produce class diagram: processor, editor, DSP modules, parameter layout, state management. Rules: APVTS for all parameters, processBlock thread-safe, Editor talks to Processor ONLY through APVTS, DSP modules are self-contained with prepare()/reset()/process() lifecycle.
items.reference: JUCE classes: https://docs.juce.com/master/classes.html — AudioProcessor, AudioProcessorValueTreeState, AudioProcessorEditor

items.title: Specify DSP algorithms with math
items.description: For each DSP block: algorithm choice, mathematical description, JUCE implementation path, CPU cost, known gotchas. VERIFY all formulas at boundary conditions.
items.prevention_rule: EM-08: Plan specified Q constant 24.5f when correct value was 49.5f. Always compute formula output at param=0 and param=1 to verify range.
items.reference: Stanford 320c: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/ — Cytomic TPT SVF papers: https://cytomic.com/files/dsp/

items.title: Break into ordered task list with code
items.description: Each task: ONE thing, files to modify, JUCE classes used, ACTUAL CODE for every step, build command, commit message. Ordered by dependency.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session2: Plan was 1577 lines — too large for single response. Write in chunks using Write + Edit. Use unique anchor strings to avoid multi-match errors.

items.title: Plan self-review
items.description: Check: scope completeness, dependency order, type consistency across tasks, formula correctness at boundary values, buffer sizes at max sample rate.
items.prevention_rule: EM-03/04/08: Plan self-review MISSED FHT placement, buffer overflow, and Q constant errors. Self-review is necessary but NOT sufficient — two-stage review during implementation catches what self-review misses.

items.title: PHASE GATE: Plan approved
gate_conditions: Every spec requirement has a corresponding task
Each task has complete code and build step
All DSP formulas verified at boundary conditions
Buffer sizes computed for max supported sample rate (192kHz)

checklists.title: Phase 3: Project Setup & Test Framework
checklists.purpose: Set up build system, test framework, and CI before writing DSP code.

items.title: Update CMakeLists.txt
items.description: Version, source files, JUCE modules, target formats (VST3 + Standalone at minimum), C++17, COPY_PLUGIN_AFTER_BUILD.
items.reference: JUCE CMake API: https://docs.juce.com/master/index.html — see also awesome-juce for CMake templates: https://github.com/sudara/awesome-juce

items.title: Set up automated test framework
items.description: Add Catch2 or GoogleTest to the project. At minimum: compilation test, parameter range tests, processBlock smoke test (no crash with silence, noise, extreme parameters). Reference melatonin blog for JUCE testing setup.
items.reference: Melatonin blog — testing with Catch2: https://melatonin.dev/blog/ — awesome-juce testing section: https://github.com/sudara/awesome-juce
tests_to_implement: Parameter range validation — all params within declared range
processBlock smoke test — 1 second of silence, no NaN/inf in output
processBlock noise test — 1 second of white noise, no NaN/inf
processBlock extreme params — all params at min, all at max, no crash
State save/restore round-trip — save state, restore, all params match

items.title: Set up CI (optional but recommended)
items.description: GitHub Actions workflow: build on Linux (required), macOS (recommended), Windows (recommended). Run automated tests after build.
items.reference: Melatonin blog — GitHub Actions for JUCE: https://melatonin.dev/blog/ — awesome-juce CI section: https://github.com/sudara/awesome-juce

items.title: PHASE GATE: Project setup complete
gate_conditions: CMakeLists.txt configured for all target formats
Test framework integrated and basic tests pass

checklists.title: Phase 4: Core DSP Implementation
checklists.purpose: Build the audio engine module by module with two-stage review after each.
pre_flight_checks: EM-03: In any FDN implementation, verify mixing matrix is in FEEDBACK path, not just output
EM-04: Compute max delay length at 192kHz: max_base * (192000/48000). Buffer must be >= this.
EM-06: All circular buffer indices use & mask wrapping
EM-08: Verify filter Q mapping at reso=0 and reso=1

items.title: Implement DSP modules with two-stage review
items.description: For EACH module: (1) dispatch implementer, (2) spec compliance review, (3) code quality review, (4) if issues: fix + re-review BOTH stages. Code quality reviewer catches what spec reviewer misses — do NOT skip it.
items.prevention_rule: EM-03: Code quality reviewer caught FHT not in feedback path (critical). EM-04: Caught buffer overflow. EM-05/06/07: Caught 3 GlitchEngine bugs. Spec reviewer alone would have missed all of these.
items.reference: DSP algorithms: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/courses/320c/ — Cytomic SVF: https://cytomic.com/files/dsp/

items.title: Run automated tests after each module
items.description: After each DSP module implementation, run the test suite. At minimum: compilation succeeds, processBlock smoke test passes.
items.validation: All tests green before proceeding to next module

items.title: PHASE GATE: All DSP modules implemented and reviewed
gate_conditions: Each module passed two-stage review (spec + code quality)
All critical and important issues resolved

checklists.title: Phase 5: Preset Data & State Management
checklists.purpose: Implement presets AND state save/restore. State persistence is NOT optional.

items.title: Implement state save/restore
items.description: CRITICAL: getStateInformation and setStateInformation must be implemented, not empty stubs. All parameters serialize and deserialize via APVTS. Test: save project in Reaper, close, reopen — all parameters restored.
items.prevention_rule: Gap analysis: Epiphany Machine v3 shipped with empty stubs. Broken state save = lost presets = angry users.
items.reference: JUCE tutorial: https://juce.com/learn/tutorials/ — 'Saving and loading your plug-in state'

items.title: Update PresetData with preset values
items.description: Add new fields to preset struct, populate preset values from spec. Preset VALUES are AI-generated from spec descriptions but must be auditioned by user in Phase 9.

items.title: Update PresetManager
items.description: Add new params to capture/apply. Use log-space interpolation for frequency params, cosine for mix. Choice params snap at 50%. Bools not morphed.
items.prevention_rule: EM-14: Use equal-power (cosine) mixing for dry/wet, not linear. Linear concentrates audible change in low end.

items.title: PHASE GATE: Presets and state management complete
gate_conditions: Preset count consistent across PresetData, APVTS, PresetManager
Morph interpolation uses log-space for frequencies, cosine for mix

checklists.title: Phase 6: Processor Integration
checklists.purpose: Wire DSP modules together in processBlock.
pre_flight_checks: EM-13: EVERY SmoothedValue must have getNextValue() called per-sample. Audit ALL SmoothedValue declarations.
EM-09: Copy formula constants from spec exactly — no rounding
EM-10: Every feedback loop must have a safety limiter (soft-clip or hard-clip)
EM-11: getTailLengthSeconds() must return max decay parameter value
EM-15: Default decay should be ≤2.0s so parameter changes are audible quickly

items.title: Update parameter layout
items.description: All parameters with correct ranges, defaults, skew values. Frequency params: skew 0.3. Decay/feedback: skew 0.5.

items.title: Implement processBlock
items.description: Full signal flow per spec. CRITICAL: after writing processBlock, audit every SmoothedValue — grep for getNextValue() in per-sample loops. Any missing = dead parameter.
items.prevention_rule: EM-13: driveSmoothed.getNextValue() was never called — drive was permanently zero. NOT caught by any reviewer, only by user in DAW testing.

items.title: SmoothedValue audit
items.description: After processBlock is written, list every SmoothedValue in the header. For each one, verify getNextValue() is called in a per-sample loop. If ANY is missing, it's a critical silent bug.
items.checklist:
For each SmoothedValue:
□ Declared in header
□ Initialized in prepareToPlay with setCurrentAndTargetValue()
□ setTargetValue() called once per block
□ getNextValue() called per-sample in a loop
□ Value used downstream (getCurrentValue() or the return from getNextValue())

items.title: PHASE GATE: Processor integration complete
gate_conditions: SmoothedValue audit: every SmoothedValue has getNextValue() per-sample

checklists.title: Phase 7: GUI / Editor Implementation
checklists.purpose: Build the visual interface. You direct look and feel, AI implements.

items.title: Define GUI layout and visual identity
items.ai_role: interviewer — ask about preferences, then implement
items.description: YOU define: dimensions, layout, visual style, colors, typography, metering. AI implements. Reference: v2 spec template has a complete GUI design section with ASCII layout, color palette, and component specs.
items.reference: JUCE GUI: https://docs.juce.com/master/classes.html — Component, LookAndFeel_V4, Slider, Label, TextButton

items.title: Implement custom LookAndFeel
items.description: Subclass LookAndFeel_V4. Apply to top-level editor. Use juce::Colour for theming.

items.title: Build component hierarchy
items.description: Every parameter control uses APVTS Attachment. Timer-based updates for value labels. setBounds layout with verified arithmetic.
items.prevention_rule: EM-12: Verify ALL component bounds fit within parent panels. Walk the arithmetic: panel starts at panelY, component bottom = componentY + componentHeight, verify componentBottom - panelY ≤ panelHeight.

items.title: Visual polish iteration
items.ai_role: implementer — you direct, AI makes changes
items.description: Load plugin, look at it, describe changes. Timebox: 2 sessions max. Ship what you have.

items.title: PHASE GATE: GUI complete
gate_conditions: All parameters have GUI controls with APVTS attachments
All controls visible and within bounds
YOU have approved the visual design

checklists.title: Phase 8: Build Verification & Cross-Platform
checklists.purpose: Verify the plugin builds and works across all target platforms and configurations.

items.title: Linux build and test
items.description: Clean build, run automated tests, verify .vst3 binary exists at expected path and size.
items.validation: cmake --build build --clean-first -- -j$(nproc) succeeds with zero errors

items.title: Cross-platform builds (macOS, Windows)
items.description: Build on macOS and Windows via CI or cross-compilation. Verify builds succeed. If no CI yet, at minimum verify the CMakeLists.txt is configured correctly for all platforms.

items.title: Sample rate stress test
items.description: Test at 44.1kHz, 48kHz, 96kHz, and 192kHz. Verify no buffer overflows, no NaN, no audio corruption.
items.prevention_rule: EM-04: DiffusionNetwork kBufSize=4096 overflowed at 96kHz+. Always test at max supported sample rate.

items.title: Buffer size stress test
items.description: Test with buffer sizes 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048. No crashes, no glitches lasting more than one buffer.

items.title: Extreme parameter test
items.description: Set all parameters to minimum, process audio. Set all to maximum, process audio. No crashes, no NaN, no inf.

items.title: Multi-instance test
items.description: Instantiate 4+ instances simultaneously. No cross-talk, no shared state corruption.
items.prevention_rule: EM-session3: static int lastPreset was shared across instances.

items.title: State save/restore in DAW
items.description: Save Reaper project with plugin loaded, close, reopen. All parameters match saved state.

items.title: Git tag release
items.description: Tag with version number: git tag vX.Y.Z

items.title: PHASE GATE: Build verified
gate_conditions: Linux build succeeds with zero errors

checklists.title: Phase 9: DAW Testing & Sound Approval
checklists.purpose: Load in Reaper, LISTEN, and fix what you find. This is where real bugs surface and YOU approve the sound.

items.title: Load in Reaper and play audio
items.description: Load plugin on a track in Reaper, play audio through it, describe what you hear. This is YOUR moment — AI cannot evaluate sound.

items.title: Control responsiveness check
items.description: Move every knob while audio plays. Does each one produce an audible/visible change? Report any that seem dead or delayed.
items.prevention_rule: EM-13: DRIVE knob was dead because SmoothedValue never advanced. EM-15: Controls seemed delayed because 4.0s default decay masked changes.

items.title: Mix range check
items.description: Sweep mix 0→1. Is the change evenly distributed, or bunched at one end?
items.prevention_rule: EM-14: Linear mix blend concentrated change in first 30% of range. Equal-power cosine mixing fixes this.

items.title: Preset audition
items.description: Load EVERY preset. For each one: does it sound good? Does it showcase the plugin's range? Is it usable? Mark any that need tuning. AI adjusts values per your direction.
items.prevention_rule: Gap analysis: Presets were AI-generated but never auditioned. Some may be unusable.

items.title: Automation test
items.description: In Reaper: record automation on 2-3 parameters, play back. Verify: no clicks, no zippers, smooth transitions.

items.title: Bypass and freeze test
items.description: Toggle bypass — clean click-free transition? Toggle freeze — infinite sustain without explosion? Freeze + high drift + high feedback — does safety limiter work?

items.title: Diagnose and fix reported issues
items.description: For each issue user reports: read processBlock, trace signal flow, identify root cause, implement fix, rebuild, user re-tests.

items.title: PHASE GATE: DAW-validated and sound-approved
gate_conditions: Plugin loads in Reaper without crashing
EVERY control produces audible/visible change when moved
Mix knob effective across full range
ALL presets auditioned — usable ones approved, broken ones fixed or removed
No audio glitches, clicks, or dropouts

checklists.title: Phase 10: Release & Distribution
checklists.purpose: Package, copy binary, push to repo.

items.title: Copy binary to project root
items.description: cp the compiled .so/.vst3 to project root for easy GitHub download. Commit it.
items.reference: Memory: project_release_workflow.md — after every build, copy .so to root

items.title: Update documentation
items.description: At minimum: what the plugin does, system requirements, install instructions per OS, parameter reference, quick start guide. If a manual exists from previous version, update it.
items.reference: Gap analysis: v2 manual may need updating for v3 changes

items.title: Push to GitHub
items.description: Push all commits + tag. If remote has diverged, pull first, resolve conflicts, then push.
items.prevention_rule: EM-16: Always git pull before pushing a large batch. For binary merge conflicts, use git checkout --ours or --theirs explicitly.

items.title: PHASE GATE: Release published
gate_conditions: Binary at project root (Linux .so at minimum)

checklists.title: Phase 11: Optimization & Hardening
checklists.purpose: Make it fast and stable. Profile before optimizing.

items.title: CPU profiling
items.description: Profile processBlock with perf (Linux), Instruments (macOS), or VTune. Identify top 3 hotspots. Do NOT optimize without profiling first.
targets: Per-sample transcendental functions (pow, sin, tan, exp) — pre-compute per block where possible
Cache-unfriendly access patterns in delay line arrays
Unnecessary computations when parameters haven't changed
items.reference: JUCE performance: https://docs.juce.com/master/index.html — juce_dsp SIMD section

items.title: Memory audit
items.description: Verify: no heap allocations in processBlock (use RAII/smart pointers), no memory leaks, all buffers pre-allocated in prepareToPlay.
items.reference: Melatonin blog — audio thread debugging: https://melatonin.dev/blog/

items.title: Denormal stress test
items.description: Process 60 seconds of silence. CPU should remain near-zero. If it spikes, denormal protection is insufficient. Use BOTH ScopedNoDenormals AND 1e-18 offset in feedback paths.

items.title: Sound verification after optimization
items.description: LISTEN after every optimization. Confirm sound hasn't changed. Never sacrifice sound quality for CPU.

items.title: PHASE GATE: Optimized and hardened
gate_conditions: Denormal stress test passes (60s silence, CPU stable)

checklists.title: Phase 12: Retrospective & Reusable Components
checklists.purpose: What worked, what didn't, extract templates for next plugin.

items.title: Process retrospective
items.description: Review: which phases took longest and why, where did AI produce best code on first try, where did most iteration cycles burn, what to add to this playbook.

items.title: Extract reusable components
items.description: Identify code worth keeping: custom DSP blocks, LookAndFeel, APVTS boilerplate, build config, test framework setup. Save as template project or personal JUCE module.

items.title: Update this playbook
items.description: Add lessons learned, new failure modes, updated prevention rules. Each plugin build should improve the playbook.

items.title: Define v2 scope (optional)
items.description: Features cut from v1, user feedback, new ideas, deferred improvements. This becomes Phase 0 input for next run.

juce_patterns.description: Reusable JUCE API patterns. Reference: https://docs.juce.com/master/classes.html

gotchas: NormalisableRange skew: 0.5 for decay/feedback-like, 0.3 for cutoff frequencies
AudioParameterChoice stores 0-based index integers, not strings
Parameter ranges must be consistent between APVTS, PresetData, and DSP code

smoothed_values.critical_rule: EVERY SmoothedValue MUST have getNextValue() called per-sample in processBlock. getCurrentValue() alone does NOT advance the smoother.
smoothed_values.code_pattern:
prepareToPlay: sm.reset(sr, 0.02); sm.setCurrentAndTargetValue(init);
processBlock: sm.setTargetValue(val); // once per block
loop: const float v = sm.getNextValue(); // per sample
Ramp times: 0.02s (20ms) for continuous params (gain, freq, mix). 0.042s (42ms) for bypass/mode transitions. Snap with setCurrentAndTargetValue() only in prepareToPlay or state load.
smoothed_values.prevention_rule: EM-13: driveSmoothed stuck at 0.0 forever because getNextValue() was never called. Silent bug — no crash, no error, just a dead control.

gotchas: Store as unique_ptr member — if it goes out of scope, the connection breaks

rules: prepare(): allocate buffers, compute coefficients from sample rate
process(): in-place stereo, no allocations, no I/O
No heap allocations (new, malloc, vector resize, string construction)
std::unordered_map::find() can allocate via std::string key construction — use flat arrays for audio-thread lookups
NEVER use juce::AsyncUpdater from audio thread — it is NOT lock-free. Use std::atomic<bool> + Timer or VBlankAttachment instead
setOpaque(true) when component fills its bounds completely — prevents parent repaint cascade
setBufferedToImage(true) for expensive static visuals (leaf components only)
Use JUCE_ENABLE_REPAINT_DEBUGGING=1 during development to visualize repaints
JUCE 7.0.6+: Use juce::VBlankAttachment instead of Timer for frame-synced UI updates
JUCE_LIVE_CONSTANT(value) provides runtime slider UI to adjust values without recompiling — use for shadow blur, spacing, opacity, color tuning during development
Treat paint() like audio thread — minimize allocations, pre-allocate Path/Image/ColourGradient as members

cross_platform.macos: AU cache reset: killall -9 AudioComponentRegistrar. Notarization required for macOS 10.15+. Universal binary: CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES 'arm64;x86_64'
cross_platform.windows: Statically link MSVC runtime: set(CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY 'MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>'). Required to avoid DLL dependency issues on end-user machines.
cross_platform.linux: VST3 path: ~/.vst3/. Build deps: libasound2-dev libjack-jackd2-dev libfreetype-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxinerama-dev libxcursor-dev

equal_power.formula: dryGain = cos(mix * PI/2); wetGain = sin(mix * PI/2);
equal_power.why: Linear blend concentrates change in low end. Equal-power keeps perceived level constant.
equal_power.prevention_rule: EM-14: ALWAYS use equal-power, not linear.

dsp_catalog.name: DiffusionNetwork (FDN Reverb)
dsp_catalog.algorithm: 8-line FDN with Fast Hadamard Transform in feedback path, RT60 decay, per-line stereo panning with LFOs
prevention_rules: EM-03: FHT must be in feedback path
dsp_catalog.reference: Julius O. Smith — Physical Audio Signal Processing: https://ccrma.stanford.edu/~jos/

dsp_catalog.name: Cytomic TPT State Variable Filter
dsp_catalog.algorithm: Trapezoidal SVF (Andy Simper). g=tan(pi*fc/sr), stable at all frequencies, no modulation clicks.
dsp_catalog.critical_note: DO NOT use Chamberlin SVF (f=2*sin(...)). It is unstable at high frequencies and clicks during modulation.
dsp_catalog.reference: Cytomic papers: https://cytomic.com/files/dsp/ — Vadim Zavalishin: The Art of VA Filter Design

dsp_catalog.name: Granular Engine
dsp_catalog.algorithm: Circular-buffer grain playback with adaptive envelopes (Hann >50ms, Tukey 10-50ms, Trapezoid <10ms)
prevention_rules: EM-07: No drift on reverse grains

dsp_catalog.name: Wavefolder
dsp_catalog.algorithm: output = input + drive * (sin(input * foldAmt * PI) / foldAmt - input). True bypass at drive=0.
prevention_rules: EM-09: Copy constants exactly from spec
EM-10: Feedback loop needs safety limiter after wavefolder

failure_modes.description: 16 bugs from Epiphany Machine v3 development. Uses EM-xx namespace (Epiphany Machine session bugs) to distinguish from FM-xx (generic JUCE failure modes in juce-failure-modes.md). Each has a prevention rule that appears as a pre-flight check or checklist item in the relevant phase. See juce-failure-modes.md 'Numbering Systems' section for cross-reference mapping.

summary_table.short: Cache keyed on names not IDs — still O(N)
FHT at output only, not in feedback — not a real FDN
Buffer overflow at >48kHz — kBufSize too small
Drift on reverse grains — out-of-window reads
Q constant wrong — 24.5 gives Q=25 not Q=50
SmoothedValue getNextValue() never called — dead parameter
Linear mix blend — only first 30% effective
Default decay too long — masks parameter changes

failure_modes.key_insight: EM-13, EM-14, EM-15 were caught by USER in DAW testing, not by any automated review. Two-stage review catches implementation bugs but cannot catch perceptual/UX issues. DAW testing by the human is irreplaceable.

when_to_start_fresh: After 3-4 implementation tasks (subagent transcripts fill context)
When API errors (529) indicate context too large
When switching from implementation to DAW testing
what_to_carry_forward: Specific pending issues with symptoms and fixes
what_to_drop: Full source file contents (AI re-reads them)

model_selection.sonnet: Plan writing and implementation execution — reliable and sufficient for all implementation
model_selection.haiku: AVOID for scoped implementation tasks — prone to scope creep (modified out-of-scope files in session)

token_saving: One task per subagent — clean context
Spec + current task section as context — not the whole plan
Let AI re-read files instead of pasting

how_to_run_this: 1. New session (Opus). Paste Phase 0 + brainstorming skill. AI asks questions, you answer. Output: spec doc.
2. New session (Sonnet). Paste spec + Phase 2 + writing-plans skill. Output: task-level plan.
3. If upgrading: run Phase 1 (perf audit). If new plugin: skip to Phase 3.
4. Phase 3: Set up build, tests, CI.
5. Phases 4-7: one session per 3-4 tasks. Use subagent-driven-development.
6. Phase 8: Build verification and stress tests.
7. Phase 9: Load in Reaper and LISTEN. Fix what you find.
